insights.title: Rain is more than crops can use
insights.body: Rain exceeds crop water demand by about 1717 mm a year. Waterlogging and runoff are bigger risks than drought.

insights.title: Fields are greenest in February, barest in November
insights.body: Satellite greenness of the farmland here peaks at 0.75 and drops to 0.44 (0 = bare, 1 = dense crop). The low months are when soil is most exposed to rain and wind.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Chickpea, Mixed vegetables and Pigeon pea score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: More downpours: about 37 heavy-rain days a year by 2035
consequences.detail: Up from about 29 today. Each downpour on bare soil washes away topsoil and the fertiliser in it; fields here are barest in Oct, Nov and Dec.
consequences.action: Keep the ground covered (a legume or crop residue) through the rainy months.

consequences.headline: +0.5 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 18.1 °C to about 18.6 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.
